title: The Lesson I Learned From Moses’ Excuses
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned From Moses’ Excuses
The Day God Called Him Changed Everything—But Not Before Moses Tried to Talk His Way Out of Destiny
There is a moment in almost every believer’s life when God places something in front of them that feels impossibly bigger than they are.
And in that moment, many of us respond exactly the same way.
Not because we lack faith entirely.
But because deep down we are painfully aware of our weaknesses.
That is why the story of Moses feels so personal.
Because Moses was not standing on a mountain when God called him.
He was hiding in a desert.
Forty years earlier, Moses had been a prince of Egypt. Then came the scandal.
Everything he thought his life would become disappeared.
If Moses had social media, people would have called him disqualified.
But God specializes in finding people in the ashes of their own mistakes.
That is why our theme has always been true:
When Moses encountered the burning bush, God revealed Himself with words that still shake history.

Literal meaning:
"I Am Who I Am" or "I Will Be What I Will Be."
The God who exists independently of all creation was speaking directly to a broken shepherd.
The God who created galaxies was calling a man who barely believed in himself.
And what happened next may be one of the most relatable conversations in all of Scripture.
"Who am I that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?"
But God never answered Moses by boosting his self-esteem.
God answered by redirecting his attention.
Many believers spend years waiting until they feel qualified enough to obey.
But Scripture repeatedly shows that God calls people before they feel ready.
"What if they ask who sent me?"
The Christian life has never been built on having all the answers.
It has always been built on trusting the One who does.
Sometimes we delay obedience because we want clarity.
Yet God often provides clarity through obedience.
The third excuse reveals something even deeper.
Fear of rejection is one of humanity's oldest struggles.
Moses imagined failure before he ever took a step.
How many dreams die the same way?
How many believers remain silent because they already decided people will not listen?
Yet God responded by giving signs that demonstrated His power.
Because the mission was never supposed to depend upon Moses' ability to convince people.
The fourth excuse cuts even closer to home.
"O my Lord, I am not eloquent."
The Hebrew expression suggests difficulty with speech.
Whether Moses had a speech impediment, lacked confidence, or simply felt inadequate, the point remains the same.
He believed his weakness disqualified him.
Many Christians still believe that lie.
"I know exactly what you lack. I created you anyway."
God is not surprised by our weaknesses.
He already accounted for them before He called us.
The final excuse exposed the real issue.
"O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send."
This is where the story becomes uncomfortable.
Because Moses had moved beyond insecurity.
And if we are honest, we have all been there.
We say we need more time.
Yet sometimes what we really mean is:
Still, the grace of God appears.
Because God's grace does not merely forgive us.
The New Testament uses the Greek word χάρις (charis) for grace.
Yet biblical grace is never passive.
Grace turns broken stories into redemptive ones.
Moses arrived at the burning bush as a shepherd hiding from his past.
The man making excuses became the man confronting Pharaoh.
The man doubting his voice became the man delivering God's Word.
The man afraid of failure became the man through whom God parted the sea.
And that is why Moses' story points beyond Moses.
Because every excuse Moses made ultimately finds its answer in Christ.
You are someone for whom Christ died.
He sent His Son so you could be part of His mission.
Jesus did not come for people who had everything together.
The people everyone else had given up on.
The Gospel is not the story of impressive people earning God's favor.
The Gospel is the story of a holy God extending mercy through Jesus Christ.
That is why no excuse is stronger than His grace.
No past is stronger than His redemption.
No failure is stronger than His forgiveness.
No weakness is stronger than His power.
Maybe you are reading this while carrying your own excuses.
Moses once felt the same way.
Yet God looked beyond every excuse and saw the leader Moses would become.
Today, through Christ, God still rewrites stories.
And perhaps the greatest lesson Moses ever taught us is this:
God is not looking for perfect people.
God is looking for willing people.
The question is not whether you have excuses.
The question is whether you will surrender them.
Because the moment Moses stopped arguing and started obeying, history changed.
And perhaps your story is waiting for the same moment.
Be honest. This hit harder than some expected.
The excuse that almost kept Moses from his calling became the testimony that proved God's power.
